criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a new test queues six person-filed urgent requests and two Steward requests, builds the plan, and asserts the first three dispatched items include at least one Steward request.
criteria.evidence: plan::tests::improvement_turn_puts_a_steward_request_among_the_first_three_dispatches passed. It first shows that build_capped leaves s1 and s2 last. It then asserts that build_improving gives order u1,u2,s1,u3,u4,s2,u5,u6, with turns at positions 3 and 6, both with no caps and with caps 3/10 where a person set all six urgents. The replan simulation and the since_turn tests passed too (7 tests in all).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a new test gives a Hestia request whose failure class appears in introspections of three distinct jobs and asserts it is ordered as urgent; a companion case with two distinct jobs asserts it is not promoted.
criteria.evidence: hestia::tests::improvement_of_feeds_the_plan_so_a_three_job_request_is_ordered_as_urgent files the request through the real error_review path. With jobs a, b, c the Hestia request is ordered first, at Urgent, with promoted.jobs == 3. With jobs a and b it stays Normal and is not promoted. The plan-level repeat_urgent tests also cover 2 versus 3 jobs, a person-set priority, and demotion when the urgent tier is full. All passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a new test with no Steward or Hestia requests queued asserts the plan order is identical to the order before the change, and the existing plan tests still pass.
criteria.evidence: build_improving_without_improvement_items_equals_build_capped asserts the whole result equals build_capped for a mixed set (with refused and held items) under both cap settings, including when the improvement ids are absent or refused. It passed. The drain test with_no_improvement_request_queued_the_order_and_the_report_are_unchanged also passed. The full suite passed in Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` (CI run 42338283026).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`: a test of the `athena plan` output (display::plan or the CLI drain test) asserts it names each item that takes the improvement turn, and that the drain report lists them.
criteria.evidence: the_plan_text_names_each_item_that_takes_the_improvement_turn_and_each_promotion calls drain::plan and display::plan. It asserts 'h1 · title of h1 takes the improvement turn at dispatch 3', the matching line for s1 at dispatch 6, and a promoted line. the_drain_dispatches_in_the_order_the_plan_showed... asserts that the run order equals the plan shown, that report.improvement_turns is [(h1,3),(s1,6)], and that display::drain prints both 'improvement' lines. The display unit tests and the parallel concurrent test also passed.

criteria.criterion: An improvement request whose reading fails (missing goal, rung or acceptance) or whose dependency is unmet is not given a turn; a test or the diff in plan.rs shows the turn is taken only from ready, passing entries.

summary: The change does what the request asks, and I recommend it pass. While a ready, passing Steward or Hestia request is queued, the planner now gives it at least one dispatch in every three, and the drain keeps that spacing each time it replans. A request whose cause is recorded in three or more distinct jobs is raised to urgent in memory only. This happens before the priority caps apply, so a full urgent tier can still demote it, and a priority a person set is never changed. `athena plan` prints a `turn` line for each item given the turn and a `promoted` line for each raised request, and the drain report lists the turns taken. I ran the new tests myself and all passed: `cargo test -p athena-core improvement_turn`, `repeat_urgent`, `improvement_of` and `build_improving_without_improvement_items_equals_build_capped`; `cargo test -p athena-cli improvement`; and the drain-report test. They cover the six-urgent-plus-two-Steward case, the 3-job versus 2-job promotion, an unchanged order when no improvement request is queued, skipping requests whose reading fails or whose dependency is unmet, and the plan and report text. Without the change these tests do not compile, so they cannot pass on the old code. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's recorded checks. The CHANGELOG matches the diff, and only the expected files changed. Two minor points remain. A person's request that cites a repeated cause or holds a spec line also counts as an improvement request. Hestia's throughput slowdown request gets no turn, because no record links it to the review; this gap is documented in the code and the CHANGELOG.
